title: Conditioned Tail Lengths in Random-Function Components
summary: The attack analysis treats conditioned and unconditioned tail-length distributions as alike, with only small-scale experimental support; rigorous bounds and the impact of discrepancies remain open.

formal_statement.body: In the random-function model underlying the duplex-based AEAD attack, compare the tail-length distribution of a random point conditioned on belonging to an $(s,\nu)$-component with the tail-length distribution of an unconditioned random point. The existing success analysis assumes that these distributions are the same to obtain a lower bound $p_{\ell}s$ on the probability that $P_{\beta}^{\ell-1}(x_0)$ belongs to the cycle, where $s$ is the component parameter and $p_{\ell}$ is the corresponding reach-the-cycle probability; small-scale experiments support this assumption, but do not establish it. The unresolved task is to characterize or rigorously bound the conditioned tail-length distribution and quantify how any difference changes the attack's success probability.

scope.domain: Random-function component and tail-length statistics in duplex-based AEAD cryptanalysis.
assumptions: A random point conditioned on belonging to an (s, ν)-component has the same tail-length distribution as an unconditioned random point.
parameters: s — component parameter and multiplicative factor in the success lower bound
ν — second descriptor of the conditioned component
ℓ — iteration index associated with the cycle-reaching event
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize or rigorously bound the conditioned tail-length distribution and quantify how deviations from the unconditioned distribution affect the attack's success probability.

citations.label: Generic Attack on Duplex-Based AEAD Modes using Random Function Statistics

progress.summary: The paper bases its success lower bound on an unproved equality of tail-length distributions while noting that strict equality is unlikely. Small-scale experiments support sufficient closeness, but no rigorous characterization or bound is established.
citation_labels: Henri Gilbert et al., Generic Attack on Duplex-Based AEAD Modes using Random Function Statistics
